getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.description: Overview of Velbok and how your studio uses the platform.

sections.heading: What is Velbok?
paragraphs: Velbok is a cloud-based studio management platform for tattoo and piercing shops. It combines scheduling, client records, deposits, consent forms, invoicing, messaging, and a customer portal in one application.
Your team signs in at the studio app (/auth). Clients interact through optional customer accounts and secure links for deposits and consent.

sections.heading: Who uses what
bullets: Studio owners & admins — full access, billing, permissions, settings
Artists — schedule, clients, stencils, deposits (based on permissions)
Front desk / assistants — schedule and inbox (when granted)
Customers — portal for bookings, payments, consent, and messages

sections.heading: First login
paragraphs: Use the email and password provided when your studio was onboarded. If you forgot your password, use Forgot password on the login page (requires email to be configured for your instance).
After login, staff are routed to the schedule. Customers are routed to their account portal.

pos-checkout.title: POS checkout & Tap to Pay
pos-checkout.description: Take in-person card payments with your phone — no separate card reader required — or with a WisePad.

sections.heading: No separate card reader required
paragraphs: Velbok supports Stripe Tap to Pay: your staff phone becomes the payment terminal. The customer holds a contactless card or their mobile wallet near the top of your device — the same way they would tap on a shop terminal.

You do not need to buy a WisePad or other Stripe hardware for this mode. Tap to Pay uses Stripe Terminal in the background (connection token and a Terminal location on your studio’s Stripe Connect account), but no physical reader is paired or registered in Stripe Dashboard.
Use the Velbok mobile app (Android or iPhone), open Checkout, choose Tap to Pay (this phone), tap Enable phone payments, then Charge as usual.

sections.heading: What customers can pay with
bullets: Contactless debit and credit cards (tap)
Google Pay (Android)
Apple Pay (iPhone and many Android wallets)
Samsung Pay and other NFC mobile wallets
Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover contactless (region-dependent)
sections.note: Wallet payments usually do not need a PIN. Some high-value or regional card rules may require a PIN or a different payment method — Velbok will show Stripe’s on-screen prompt if that happens.

sections.heading: Stripe setup (no hardware purchase)
bullets: Finish Stripe Connect for your studio (Admin → POS checkout)
Create a Terminal location in Velbok — Admin → POS → Create Terminal location (Velbok saves this on your Connect account)
Enable POS checkout for staff
Install the release Velbok app on a compatible phone — not a debug build. Download from https://velbok.com/download
There is no separate “enable Tap to Pay” switch in Stripe for Velbok; you only need Connect + Terminal location
You only register a reader serial number in Stripe Dashboard if you use a physical device (e.g. WisePad 3)

sections.heading: Supported Android phones (Tap to Pay)
paragraphs: Stripe maintains the authoritative list; Velbok follows the same requirements. Phones must have NFC, Android 13+, Google Play Services, and Stripe’s security hardware (hardware keystore with ECDH). Developer options must be OFF for live payments.
bullets: Google Pixel — Pixel 6 and newer (6, 6a, 6 Pro, 7 series, 8 series, 9 series, 10 series, Pixel Fold)
Samsung Galaxy S — S22, S22+, S22 Ultra, S23 series, S24 series, S25 series, S26 series
Samsung Galaxy Z — Z Flip4, Z Flip5, Z Flip6, Z Flip7, Z Flip7 FE, Z Fold4, Z Fold5, Z Fold6, Z Fold7, Z TriFold
Samsung Galaxy A / M / F — many recent models (e.g. A14 5G and newer A-series, A53 5G+, M14 5G+, F34 5G+) — see Stripe link below for the full list
Samsung — Tab Active5 series, XCover7, XCover7 Pro, Wide8
Motorola — edge series (2022+), razr / razr+ (2022+), many moto g models with NFC
OnePlus — 10 series and newer, Nord 3 5G+, Open
Xiaomi / Redmi — 12 series and newer, many Note 13+ / 14+ models, MIX Flip / MIX Fold
Honor, Oppo, Asus ROG/Zenfone, Infinix — numerous models listed by Stripe

sections.heading: Android phones that do NOT work
bullets: Samsung Galaxy S21, S20, S10 and older S-series flagships — missing required security hardware (confirmed: S21 Ultra fails; use S22+ or WisePad)
Any phone without NFC or without hardware keystore ECDH (Stripe error TAP_TO_PAY_UNSUPPORTED_DEVICE)
Rooted phones, emulators, or phones without Google Play Services
Android 12 or older
Debug Velbok installs or phones with Developer options ON (for live Tap to Pay)

sections.heading: iPhone (Tap to Pay on iPhone)
bullets: Compatible iPhone with NFC — generally iPhone XS or later
iOS 16.4 or later
Velbok iOS app with Apple’s Tap to Pay on iPhone entitlement (studio owner requests this from Apple for the app)
Same customer payment types: contactless cards and Apple Pay
Stripe Connect + Terminal location in Velbok Admin → POS, same as Android

sections.heading: WisePad and other readers (optional)
paragraphs: If your phone is not supported, or you prefer a dedicated device, use WisePad (Bluetooth) in Checkout. WisePOS E and Stripe Reader S700 work as Wi‑Fi/standalone readers. Register WisePad serial numbers in Stripe Dashboard → Terminal → Readers on your Connect account.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
bullets: Install the latest release APK from https://velbok.com/download — uninstall old Velbok first if needed.
Tap Test Stripe server link on Checkout to verify Connect + Terminal location before Enable
Allow Location permission for Velbok (required by Stripe Terminal on Android)
Turn Developer options OFF and restart the phone if Stripe reports an insecure environment
Galaxy S21 users: switch to WisePad mode or use a Galaxy S22+ / Z Flip7+ phone for Tap to Pay

sections.heading: Splitting payment with an artist
paragraphs: If your studio shares POS takings with resident or guest artists, both the studio and each artist need their own Stripe Connect payout account. Velbok routes the artist’s share automatically after the client pays.
See the full guide: https://velbok.com/docs/pos-split-payments — including setup steps, how turnover is recorded for tax purposes, and important accounting disclaimers.

pos-split-payments.title: POS split payments
pos-split-payments.description: Share in-person card takings between your studio and artists — Connect setup, how money moves, and what the split percentage means for your accounts.

sections.heading: What split payments do
paragraphs: When an artist is assigned on a POS charge, Velbok collects the full amount from the client on your studio’s Stripe Connect account, keeps your configured shop share in that account, and transfers the artist’s share to the artist’s own Connect account.

The split percentage controls how much each party receives in Stripe — it does not mean each party only declares that percentage of the client payment for tax or turnover purposes. See Turnover and subcontractor model below.

sections.heading: Both studio and artist need a Connect account
paragraphs: Split payouts only work when two separate Stripe Connect accounts exist and are fully onboarded:
1. Your studio (shop) — receives the client payment and holds the shop share.
2. Each artist who receives a split — receives their share by transfer into their own Connect account.

If either account is missing, incomplete, or was created outside Velbok’s Connect platform, the artist transfer will fail even though the client was charged successfully. Retry is available from Admin → POS checkout after the artist finishes setup.
sections.note: Artists must onboard through Velbok (Settings → POS payout account). A Stripe account ID copied from another platform or an old personal Connect account will not work.

sections.heading: Studio setup (shop Connect account)
bullets: Sign in as a studio admin and open Admin → POS checkout.
Complete Stripe Connect using the Payouts / Connect card on that page — identity, business details, and bank account.
Create a Terminal location (Admin → POS checkout → Create Terminal location) so Tap to Pay and card readers work.
Set the default shop split % (e.g. 50% shop / 50% artist) and enable POS checkout for staff.
Optionally set per-artist overrides: custom shop % and/or a Connect account ID if the artist has not self-served yet.
paragraphs: The studio Connect account is the merchant of record for the client payment: the customer’s receipt and card statement show your studio’s Stripe account.

sections.heading: Artist setup (payout Connect account)
bullets: The artist signs in to Velbok with their own user account (linked to your studio).
Open Settings → POS payout account.
Tap Connect payout account and complete Stripe’s Express onboarding — legal name, date of birth, address, and bank details.
Return to Velbok; the card should show Connected when payouts are enabled.
Artists can open the Stripe Express dashboard from the same card to view transfers and update bank details.
paragraphs: Each artist who receives POS splits needs their own onboarding. Guest artists need a Velbok login for your studio before they can connect.

Studio admins can still paste an artist’s Connect account ID (acct_…) under Admin → POS checkout → Artist overrides, but self-service via Settings is recommended so the account is registered on the correct Connect platform.

sections.heading: At checkout
bullets: Staff selects the artist on the POS charge (when splits are enabled for your studio).
The client pays the full amount — e.g. £200 — on the studio’s terminal or Tap to Pay.
Stripe settles the payment to the studio Connect account minus Stripe fees.
Velbok transfers the artist’s configured share (e.g. £100 at 50/50) to the artist’s Connect account.
The shop share remains in the studio Connect account.
If a transfer fails, the sale is still paid; fix Connect setup and use Admin → POS to retry the artist transfer.

sections.heading: Subcontractor model and turnover
paragraphs: Velbok is built around a common studio model: the shop supplies the client and premises, and the artist works as a subcontractor (or independent contractor) paid a fee or commission from the studio.
Under this model, the full amount the client pays at POS is normally part of the studio’s gross takings or turnover — 100% of what the customer paid, not only the shop’s split percentage.

The artist’s income for accounting purposes is usually the fee or commission the studio pays them (their split amount), not a direct share of the client’s receipt. How you label this in your books — commission, chair rent, subcontractor invoice — depends on your legal structure and local rules.
The split % in Velbok only divides money in Stripe between two Connect accounts. It does not replace payroll, invoicing, or tax reporting obligations between studio and artist.
sections.note: This description reflects how many tattoo studios operate with resident artists, similar to HMRC’s “Option B” chair-rental / commission models in other industries. Your structure may differ — confirm with a qualified adviser.

sections.heading: Tax, VAT, and accounting — important disclaimer
paragraphs: Velbok provides software to take payments and route splits between Connect accounts. We do not provide tax, VAT, accounting, or legal advice.

We are not responsible for your tax status, registrations, returns, or compliance in any country. Rules for turnover, VAT, income tax, self-employment, and subcontractor relationships vary widely — the UK, EU, US, and other jurisdictions each have different requirements.

You and your artists should speak to a qualified accountant or tax adviser about: what counts as studio turnover vs artist income, whether VAT applies to the full client payment or only part of it, how to document payments between studio and artist, and record-keeping for audits.
Stripe may issue tax forms or reporting depending on account type and region; that is between you, your artists, and Stripe — not something Velbok determines.
By using split payments you confirm that you will obtain appropriate professional advice for your situation and that Velbok is only a payment routing tool, not your tax agent or accountant.

sections.heading: SMS reminders (optional Twilio)

sections.heading: Using stencils
paragraphs: Artists with stencil permission can upload reference images and generate stencil variations in several styles, each named after a capital city — Paris signature line, London traditional, Tokyo fine line, Rome sketch, Berlin dotwork, and Madrid blackwork. Each style shows an example render you can tap to enlarge, so you can see how its lines look before generating.

AI generation is metered: each account can produce up to 10 AI stencils over any rolling 24-hour period. A live countdown shows how many generations remain, and a failed render does not count against it.

Generated stencils are kept in storage for 24 hours so they can be re-opened and re-downloaded from the Recent stencils folder, then automatically deleted. The Basic in-browser engine is free and unmetered.
sections.note: Basic mode runs entirely in the browser and is free. AI mode renders professional stencils through Netlify AI Gateway with no API keys to manage.

sms-twilio-setup.title: SMS & Twilio setup
sms-twilio-setup.description: Connect your studio's own Twilio account for SMS appointment and deposit reminders.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: SMS is not included as a Velbok-wide service. Each studio creates a Twilio account, buys a phone number, and connects it in Velbok Inbox. Twilio bills you directly for messages and number rental.
Use a dedicated number for Velbok if another service (e.g. Vapi voice AI) already controls the Twilio webhook on your existing number.

sections.heading: Step 1 — Connect in Velbok
bullets: Staff app → Inbox → SMS (Twilio) card → Connect Twilio
Enter Account SID, Auth Token, and phone number in E.164 format (+353…, +44…, +1…)
Credentials are stored per organization only

sections.heading: Step 2 — Twilio webhook
bullets: Twilio Console → Phone Numbers → your number → Messaging
A message comes in → Webhook → https://tkremoxfkgoiuwghtzwd.supabase.co/functions/v1/sms-webhook
HTTP POST. Optional Supabase secret TWILIO_SMS_WEBHOOK_URL with the same URL (no trailing slash)

sections.heading: Step 3 — SMS reminders
bullets: Admin → Emails & reminders → Notification channel → SMS or Email & SMS
Enable appointment and/or deposit reminders
Bookings need a client phone number; VIP clients skip deposit SMS

sections.heading: Testing & troubleshooting
bullets: Inbound: text your Twilio number; optional for reminder-only setups
Twilio Monitor → Messaging → webhook should return 200 when using two-way SMS
401 Invalid signature → Auth Token mismatch between Twilio and Velbok
no_matching_org → phone number in Velbok must match Twilio exactly
sections.note: Ireland (+353) numbers work well for UK/EU studios when +44 is unavailable in Twilio. Do not share Auth Tokens in support tickets.
